ēligō, ēligere, ēlēgī, ēlēctum

verb, third conjugation

Other words

  • dēligō, dēligere, dēlēgī, dēlēctum — choose out, select

    verb, third conjugation: with an accusative, often with ex · also used · classical · Plaut. Am. 1.1.49: dēlēgit virōs prīmōrēs prīncipēs (Lewis & Short); Cic. Rosc. Am. 3 fin.: quī ex senātū in hoc cōnsilium dēlēctī estis (Lewis & Short)

    Pick the best or the fittest out of a number: men for a task, a leader, a place for a camp (Lewis & Short). Not to be confused with dēligāre, “tie fast”.

Examples

  • Colōrem ēlige.

    Choose a colour.composed

See also colour, what do you want?, this one or that one?.

SourcesLewis & Short: eligo · Lewis & Short: deligo

The example sentence marked “composed” is ours.
